title: Two Sum on a Sorted List
statement:
Find two numbers in a sorted list that add up to a target, and print their positions.

The first line is the count `n` (at least 2). The second line has `n` whole numbers sorted from smallest to largest, and a number can appear more than once. The third line is the target. Exactly one pair of numbers at two different positions adds up to the target. Print the two positions counting from 1, the smaller one first, separated by a space. Aim to use only a few variables of extra memory, and go through the list once.

Input:

```text
4
2 7 11 15
9
```

Expected output:

```text
1 2
```
hints: Start with one index at each end of the list and look at the sum of the two numbers there.

The list is sorted, so moving the left index right can only make the sum bigger, and moving the right index left can only make it smaller. Decide which one to move from whether the sum is too small or too big.
Positions count from 1 here, so add 1 to each index before you print it.
